answer: When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 7 times its size, so a group of 78 keys loses far more than 78 single identities would. The river graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the quill audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the quartz checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 18 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
